newsitem.title: USA: Los Angeles police chief won't get second term.
newsitem.headline: Los Angeles police chief won't get second term.

text.p: Los Angeles Police Chief Willie Williams, hired in 1992 to improve the image of a force battered by riots and allegations of racism, will not be offered a second five-year term, the city's Police Commission announced Monday.
"He is not the appropriate person to lead the department into the next century," said Police Commission President Raymond Fisher.

Fisher said the five-member panel's decision not to renew the chief's contract was unanimous. Members concluded Williams failed to manage the Los Angeles Police Department effectively and restore morale.

Williams, the first black police chief in Los Angeles, was lured from Philadelphia to reform the LAPD following the March 1991 videotaped beating of a black man by white police officers and the resulting civil disturbances.

Last week, his lawyers had threatened to file a $3 million lawsuit against the city if his contract was not renewed. But on Monday at a news conference, Williams declined to say what action he might take, if any.

"The decision has been made and I will leave that decision as it is," he told reporters. "My actions will focus on (lobbying) the members of the city council," he said. The city council may overturn the civilian Commission's decision, but observers said there did not appear to be enough votes.
Williams said he would spend the rest of his term until July 6, talking to police officers and listening to what they feel needs to be done to improve the force.
"I have provided effective leadership for the men and women inside this organisation," he said.
But the Commission cited a special counsel's review of reforms in the LAPD saying internal management was not as "coherent or efficient" as it should be.
"The Chief has been unable to consistently maintain the reform process or to effectively provide a direction and focus for the department," said Fisher.
Despite an ability to communicate with citizens about the need for reform, Williams "has consistently not translated words into action," he said.
Mayor Richard Riordan, who has made no secret of his dislike for Williams said he supported the Commission's move.

The image of the LAPD took a battering after the beating of Rodney King, which was captured on videotape, and in 1992, when riots erupted following the acquittal of four officers on state charges. Two officers were later convicted of federal charges in the King beating.
In July 1991, the independent Christopher Commission released a report finding widespread brutality and racism in the police force and called for the resignation of Williams' predecessor Daryl Gates.
In 1992, Amnesty International accused Los Angeles police of widespread use of excessive force, sometimes amounting to torture.
And a commission headed by former FBI director William Webster, investigating police response during the riots, concluded the city was woefully unprepared and singled out Gates for blame.
Gates retired under pressure in June 1992 and Williams was sworn-in as police chief.
